trickyParts: The claim route now makes two bucket reads (the claimant's own and, for a soft claim naming a predecessor, that predecessor's), each capped at roleHolderReadTimeout = 2s and both inside the route's sendRequestBudget = 3500ms. The frozen-bus route table (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/write_routes_frozen_bus_test.go, writeRoutesWithin = 4s) is the machine check that the route still fits, and it is unchanged and green.

The claimant's bucket read is not conditional on soft: the entry it answers is also the one PutWithin writes back, so reading it only for soft claims would reinstate the stale write-back the cache gave.

DeleteIfInstance retries its conditional delete once on a lost compare-and-swap, because the common cause is the deleting instance's own heartbeat landing between the read and the delete, and a spurious 'kept' would leave the predecessor's entry alive and make the next claim a 409 for no reason. A second lost compare-and-swap answers kept.
A value in the session bucket this build cannot unmarshal names no instance, so DeleteIfInstance deletes it (logged): a record no reader can act on must not block a deregistration.

The module's run resolves undefined when a task's session moved, which is how a pass decides nothing. The two call sites that must still reject — the Legion bridge's claim and the envoy_role_set tool — turn that undefined into SessionLeftError naming the session the task was decided for, which is what their existing tests pin.

The handle's subscribe takes the dial step rather than the module's bare adapter: a subscribe that has to make the connection would otherwise dial unfenced, and a refused task would open subjects a newer pass had closed.
packages/pi-envoy/scripts/role-takeover drivers are Bun processes outside the package's test runner; they are typechecked (tsconfig.json includes them) but run only by the smoke.
